rows.n: Ōdōri Park (大通公園)
rows.w: The 1.5 km green firebreak that splits Sapporo north from south — stage of the Sapporo Snow Festival in February, beer gardens and the autumn food festival.

rows.n: Historical Village of Hokkaido (北海道開拓の村)
rows.w: Open-air museum of 50-plus relocated Meiji–early Shōwa buildings — herring lodges, farmhouses, a horse-drawn tram — telling the story of Hokkaido's settlement.

rows.n: Shiroi Koibito Park (白い恋人パーク)
rows.w: Ishiya's Tudor-style chocolate factory behind Hokkaido's most famous souvenir cookie — factory line views, cookie workshops, a free courtyard and café.
ph: Photo: 掬茶 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Sapporo Beer Museum (サッポロビール博物館)
rows.nat: サッポロビール博物館
rows.w: Japan's only beer museum, in the 1890 red-brick Sapporo Sugar Company building — the story of the oldest Japanese beer brand, with a tasting salon.
ph: Photo: K. Takeda · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Sapporo Factory (サッポロファクトリー)
rows.nat: サッポロファクトリー
rows.w: Shopping complex on the site of the first Sapporo Beer brewery — the original brick buildings plus a vast glass atrium, shops, restaurants and a cinema.

rows.n: Tsukigata Kabato Museum — former Kabato Prison (月形樺戸博物館)
rows.w: Museum in the 1886 headquarters of Kabato Shūjikan, the Meiji convict prison whose inmates cleared the Ishikari valley — irons, cells and the real men behind several Golden Kamuy convicts.
ph: Tsukigata Kabato Museum — former Kabato Prison
Photo: Totti · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Jōzankei Onsen (定山渓温泉)
rows.w: Sapporo's own hot-spring town an hour south, in a Toyohira River gorge inside Shikotsu-Tōya National Park — foot baths and autumn colour.
ph: Photo: MIKI Yoshihito from Sapporo City,Hokkaido., JAPAN · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Pokémon Center Sapporo (ポケモンセンターサッポロ)
rows.nat: ポケモンセンターサッポロ
rows.w: Hokkaido's only official Pokémon Center, on the 8th floor of Daimaru by Sapporo Station — ~2,500 items incl. Sapporo-only Pikachu goods and pins.

rows.n: Otaru Canal (小樽運河)
rows.w: The 1923 freight canal lined with stone warehouses and gas lamps — Otaru's postcard, best at dusk and during the February Snow Light Path.

rows.n: Otaru City General Museum (小樽市総合博物館)
rows.w: Hokkaido's railway birthplace — steam locomotives in the old Temiya roundhouse, plus the canal-side annex in a former warehouse.
ph: Photo: Twilight2640 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Former Aoyama Villa — Otaru Kihinkan (小樽貴賓館 旧青山別邸)
rows.nat: 小樽貴賓館 旧青山別邸
rows.w: The opulent 1923 retreat a herring-fishing dynasty built from its fortune — painted ceilings, lacquer and a peony garden.

rows.n: Goryōkaku (五稜郭)
rows.w: Japan's first Western-style fortress, the 1866 star fort where the Republic of Ezo made its last stand — a thousand cherry trees fill the moats in spring.
ph: Photo: Keihin nike · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Ōdōri Park (大通公園)
rows.w: The 1.5 km green firebreak that splits Sapporo north from south — stage of the Sapporo Snow Festival in February, beer gardens and the autumn food festival.

rows.n: Menya Saimi (麺屋彩未)
rows.w: The miso-ramen counter Sapporo queues for — three white misos over a clear pork-bone broth, a dab of grated ginger on the chāshū. Michelin Bib Gourmand (Hokkaido 2017) and Tabelog Ramen Hokkaido 100 (2024).

rows.n: Sapporo Clock Tower (札幌市時計台)
rows.w: The 1878 wooden drill hall of the Sapporo Agricultural College, its clock still striking the hours — the city's symbol and an Important Cultural Property.
ph: Photo: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Former Hokkaido Government Office (Akarenga, 赤れんが庁舎)
rows.w: The 1888 neo-baroque red-brick seat of the Hokkaido Development Commission — reopened 25 July 2025 after a multi-year restoration as a museum of Hokkaido history with a free garden.

rows.n: Moerenuma Park (モエレ沼公園)
rows.w: Isamu Noguchi's last great work: a former landfill sculpted into one park-sized artwork — Mt Moere, the Glass Pyramid, the Sea Fountain.
ph: Photo: もんもん · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Nijō Market (二条市場)
rows.w: A city block of crab, uni, ikura and fish stalls since the Meiji era, with kaisendon counters and the Noren Yokochō drinking alley.

rows.n: Hokkaido University — Poplar & Ginkgo Avenues (北海道大学 札幌キャンパス)
rows.nat: 北海道大学 札幌キャンパス
rows.w: The 1876 Sapporo Agricultural College campus, 7 minutes from the station — the 1903 Poplar Avenue (replanted after the 2004 typhoon), the ginkgo avenue, and a 1929 scratch-tile museum of 3 million specimens.
ph: Photo: T DMY · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons (resized)

rows.n: Aji no Sanpei (味の三平)
rows.w: Where miso ramen was born in 1955 — the owner took his cue from miso soup.

rows.n: Jingisukan Hitsujikai no Mise Itadakimasu (羊飼いの店 いただきます。)
rows.nat: 羊飼いの店 いただきます。
rows.w: A Susukino jingisukan run by an owner who took up shepherding to supply it — rare cuts of purebred Hokkaido Suffolk on the domed grill.

rows.n: Menya Yukikaze Susukino Honten (麺屋 雪風 すすきの本店)
rows.nat: 麺屋 雪風 すすきの本店
rows.w: No. 3 in MAPPLE's Sapporo ramen top 30 — a rich-yet-clean 'nōkō miso' of pork-bone and chicken paitan with curly medium noodles.

rows.n: Ebisoba Ichigen Sōhonten (えびそば一幻 総本店)
rows.nat: えびそば一幻 総本店
rows.w: Sapporo's prawn-ramen original, burning through ~60 kg of shrimp heads a day; pick your broth from pure shrimp to half pork-bone.

rows.n: Snow Brand Parlor Sapporo Honten (雪印パーラー 札幌本店)
rows.nat: 雪印パーラー 札幌本店
rows.w: Sapporo's 1961 dairy parlour: 30-plus parfaits and the 'Snow Royal' ice cream first made for a 1968 imperial visit.

rows.w: Sapporo's 1961 dairy parlour: 30-plus parfaits and the 'Snow Royal' ice cream first made for a 1968 imperial visit.

rows.n: Jingisukan Daruma Honten (だるま本店)
rows.w: The Susukino jingisukan room since 1954 — a cast-iron dome at every seat, one cut of mutton, sweet-spicy dipping sauce, a queue from 17:30. Cash only.

rows.n: Soup Curry Garaku (スープカレー GARAKU)
rows.w: Numbered tickets and daily lines for a soup curry whose broth borrows udon-shop dashi technique — pork bone and herbs stewed two days, kelp and bonito layered in.

rows.n: Sapporo Beer Garden (サッポロビール園)
rows.w: Restaurants spread through the garden serve fresh-lamb jingisukan and seasonal Hokkaido produce with Sapporo draught — Kessel Hall does all-you-can-eat-and-drink.

rows.n: Magic Spice Sapporo Honten (マジックスパイス 札幌本店)
rows.nat: マジックスパイス 札幌本店
rows.w: The shop that named 'soup curry' — a broth of about twenty spices built on the idea that food is medicine, ordered by escalating heat levels.

rows.n: Okushiba Shōten Ekimae Sōseiji (奥芝商店 駅前創成寺)
rows.nat: 奥芝商店 駅前創成寺
rows.w: Soup curry rebuilt around a sweet, rich shrimp-head dashi, piled with Hokkaido vegetables — the chain's station-side temple-themed branch.

rows.n: Tsukisappu Jingisukan Club (ツキサップじんぎすかんクラブ)
rows.nat: ツキサップじんぎすかんクラブ
rows.w: Fresh mutton over charcoal in clay braziers, at a ranch-side club that began in 1953 as members-only.

rows.n: Ajanta Yakuzen Curry Honpo Sōhonke (アジャンタ薬膳カリィ本舗総本家)
rows.nat: アジャンタ薬膳カリィ本舗総本家
rows.w: Ajanta's 1970s medicinal curry is where Sapporo soup curry began; this is the head shop.

rows.n: Ame wa, Yasashiku No.2 (雨は、やさしくNo.2)
rows.w: A creative Sapporo shop whose signature bowl comes with a scallop paste you stir in as you eat. rurubu's 2025 list of local favourites includes it.

rows.n: Kaiten-zushi Nemuro Hanamaru, JR Tower Stellar Place (回転寿司 根室花まる JRタワーステラプレイス店)
rows.nat: 回転寿司 根室花まる JRタワーステラプレイス店
rows.w: Sapporo Station branch of the Nemuro conveyor-belt chain, with fish shipped direct from Nemuro. Locals rank it among the city's best kaiten-zushi, and the queues are long.

rows.n: Soup Curry Picante, Kita 13-jō Honten (ピカンティ)
rows.w: One of the founding soup-curry houses (1996), by Hokkaido University — vegetable-heavy curries with a choice of rich, light or shrimp-dashi broth.

rows.n: Tanukikōji Shopping Street (狸小路商店街)
rows.w: Hokkaido's oldest shopping arcade (1873) — seven covered blocks of drugstores, souvenir shops, retro diners and the market at 7-chōme.

rows.n: Maruyama Park (円山公園)
rows.w: The city's favourite hanami park at the foot of Mount Maruyama, beside Hokkaido Shrine — barbecue under the cherries in early May, red maples in autumn.

rows.n: Hōheikan & Nakajima Park (豊平館・中島公園)
rows.w: The 1880 white-and-ultramarine Western-style imperial guesthouse, an Important Cultural Property, in the downtown park with Shōbu pond, the Hassōan teahouse and Kitara concert hall.

rows.nat: さっぽろ羊ヶ丘展望台
rows.w: The hill with the bronze of Dr William S. Clark pointing to the horizon ('Boys, be ambitious!') over sheep pasture and the Ishikari Plain.

rows.nat: 大倉山ジャンプ競技場
rows.w: The 1972 Winter Olympics large hill — ride the chairlift to the top-of-jump observatory over the city, then the Olympic Museum at its foot.

rows.n: Susukino (すすきの)
rows.w: Japan's biggest entertainment district north of Tokyo — the Nikka neon man, Ramen Yokochō, izakaya towers and the February ice-sculpture site.

rows.n: Hōheikyō Dam (豊平峡ダム)
rows.w: A 102.5 m concrete arch dam (1972) on the upper Toyohira River beyond Jōzankei — autumn colour in the Jōzankei hills.

rows.n: JR Tower Observatory T38 (JRタワー展望室 T38)
rows.w: The 38th-floor deck of the Sapporo Station tower — a 360° view down the city grid to Ōdōri and the mountains.

rows.n: Sapporo Dome (札幌ドーム)
rows.w: The silver dome stadium of football and concerts, with an observatory over the city.

rows.n: Maeda Forest Park (前田森林公園)
rows.w: A 1980s–90s landscape park whose 600 m-long, 15 m-wide canal runs dead straight toward Mt Teine.
